propositions.text: The claimant is a Haitian citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Haiti, is claiming refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a Haitian citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1), stated by the court.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant did not prove a serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned to Haiti.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that the claimant did not establish that there is a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground or that, on a balance of probabilities, the claimant would be personally subjected to a danger of torture, to a risk to her life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if she had to return to her country.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant did not prove serious persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned, stated by the court.

propositions.text: The main allegations supporting the refugee claim are summarized.
propositions.quote: The main allegations in support of the refugee protection claim are as follows:

paragraphs.summary: The court summarizes the main allegations supporting the refugee claim.

propositions.text: The claimant's stepfather was a military attaché in the Duvalier government.
propositions.quote: The claimant's stepfather was a military attaché in the Duvalier government.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's stepfather was a military attaché in the Duvalier government, as found by the earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: The claimant's mother died in July 1991; claimant then lived with grandmother and aunt.
propositions.quote: On July XXXX, 1991, her mother died. The claimant went to live with her grandmother in XXXX, and then with her aunt in Port-au-Prince.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's mother died in 1991; claimant lived with grandmother and aunt, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: In 1997, the claimant's stepfather disappeared and was rumored dead.
propositions.quote: In 1997, her stepfather disappeared and was rumoured to be dead.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's stepfather disappeared in 1997 and was rumored dead, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: After the earthquake, claimant lived in XXXX XXXX XXXX with sisters' financial help.
propositions.quote: After the earthquake, the claimant went to live in XXXX XXXX XXXX, with financial help from her sisters.

paragraphs.summary: After the earthquake, claimant lived in XXXX XXXX XXXX with sisters' financial help, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Claimant worked full-time at publishing and part-time selling clothes; criminals demanded money from her business.
propositions.quote: She worked full-time for a publishing company and part-time selling used clothing at the Tabarre market in Port-au-Prince. Criminals regularly came to demand money from her business.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant worked full-time publishing and part-time selling clothes; criminals demanded money, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Since 2009, claimant has lived alone with her daughter.
propositions.quote: Since 2009, she has lived alone with her daughter.

paragraphs.summary: Since 2009, claimant lived alone with her daughter, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: On Dec 29, 2015, two men robbed claimant at gunpoint and told her not to complain, but she did.
propositions.quote: On December 29, 2015, around 6:45 a.m., when the claimant was leaving her home to go to work, two men in hoods driving a motorbike pointed a gun at her. They stole her purse. They told her not to file a complaint, which she did.

paragraphs.summary: On Dec 29, 2015, two men robbed claimant at gunpoint and told her not to complain, but she did, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Claimant moved to XXXX XXXX neighborhood in Port-au-Prince.
propositions.quote: The claimant moved to XXXX XXXX, a neighbourhood in Port-au-Prince.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant moved to XXXX XXXX neighborhood in Port-au-Prince, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: In July 2017, five men attacked claimant at home, beat her, threatened with gun, demanded money; one attempted rape but was stopped.
propositions.quote: In July 2017, five men in hoods entered her home. She was beaten. They threatened her with a gun and demanded money from her. One of them wanted to rape her, but another one told him to forget it.

paragraphs.summary: In July 2017, five men attacked claimant at home, beat her, threatened with gun, demanded money; one attempted rape but was stopped, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: The day after the attack, claimant went to uncle's home in XXXX.
propositions.quote: The following day, the claimant went to her uncle's home in XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The day after the attack, claimant went to uncle's home in XXXX, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: On August XXXX, 2017, claimant returned to Port-au-Prince to file a complaint.
propositions.quote: On August XXXX, 2017, she returned to Port-au-Prince to file a complaint.

paragraphs.summary: On August XXXX, 2017, claimant returned to Port-au-Prince to file a complaint, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Claimant's employer offered free apartment stay.
propositions.quote: Her employer at the publishing company offered for her to stay for free in one of his apartments.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's employer offered free apartment stay, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Claimant left Haiti in August 2017 with US visa, arrived in Canada Sept 2, 2017 to claim refugee protection.
propositions.quote: Since she had a visa for the United States, the claimant decided to leave Haiti on August XXXX, 2017. She arrived in Canada on September 2, 2017, with the intention of claiming refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant left Haiti in August 2017 with US visa, arrived Canada Sept 2, 2017 to claim refugee protection, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Claimant's identity was established to panel's satisfaction by passport copy.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction through a copy of her passport filed into evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's identity established by passport copy.

propositions.text: On August 31, 2018, claimant's lawyer sent additional submissions, which panel read.
propositions.quote: On August 31, 2018, the claimant's lawyer sent the panel additional submissions, which it read.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant's lawyer sent additional submissions on August 31, 2018, which panel read.

propositions.text: Panel considered Guideline 4 on Women Refugee Claimants fearing gender-related persecution.
propositions.quote: The panel considered Guideline 4: Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the panel considered Guideline 4 on women refugee claimants fearing gender-related persecution.

propositions.text: Paragraph 97(1)(a) IRPA does not apply given evidence; claim analyzed under section 96 and subsection 97(1)(b) only.
propositions.quote: Given the evidence on the record and paragraph 97(1)(a) of the IRPA, the latter does not apply. The panel will therefore analyze the refugee protection claim under section 96 and subsection 97(1)(b) of the IRPA only.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds paragraph 97(1)(a) IRPA does not apply; claim analyzed under section 96 and subsection 97(1)(b) only.

propositions.text: The claimant was credible about being robbed in 2015, victim of break and enter in 2017, and paying criminals for her business.
propositions.quote: The claimant was credible with respect to her allegations that she was robbed in 2015, that she was the victim of a break and enter in July 2017, and that she had to give money to criminals when she had her part-time business.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant credible about being robbed in 2015, break and enter in 2017, and paying criminals for her business.

propositions.text: The panel cannot allow the refugee protection claim for the following reasons.
propositions.quote: However, the panel cannot allow the refugee protection claim for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes it cannot allow the refugee protection claim for stated reasons.

propositions.text: At hearing, claimant fears returning to Haiti because she is a single woman.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the claimant stated that she fears returning to Haiti because she is a single woman.

propositions.text: Claimant did not apply for asylum in US during 2013, 2016, 2017 trips because she had no one there and daughter was in Haiti.
propositions.quote: When asked why she did not apply for asylum in the United States during her trips in 2013, 2016 and May 2017 for vacation, given that she has been living alone with her daughter since 2009, she testified that it was because she had no one in the United States and her daughter was in Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant fears returning to Haiti as a single woman and did not seek US asylum due to no contacts and daughter in Haiti.

propositions.text: Claimant's behaviour is inconsistent with fearing return to Haiti as a single woman.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant's behaviour is inconsistent with her allegation that she fears returning to Haiti because she is a single woman.

propositions.text: Claimant has sisters in Canada who helped financially in Haiti, including one who claimed refugee protection and could have helped her come to Canada during US trips.
propositions.quote: Moreover, she has sisters in Canada who helped her financially in Haiti, including one who claimed refugee protection several years ago and, in the panel's opinion, was in a position to help her come to Canada during her trips to the United States.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's behaviour inconsistent with her fear and notes sisters in Canada helped financially and could have helped her come to Canada.

propositions.text: There is more to consider beyond previous points.
propositions.quote: But there is more.

paragraphs.summary: The court indicates there are additional considerations beyond prior points.

propositions.text: Claimant testified fear of arriving alone at Port-au-Prince airport.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified she was afraid to arrive alone at the airport in Port-au-Prince.

propositions.text: Claimant arranged for a friend to pick her up at airport after US trips.
propositions.quote: She testified that each time she returned from the United States she had arranged for a colleague and friend, Ms. XXXX, to come pick her up at the airport.

propositions.text: Claimant said she could arrange someone to pick her up if she returned to Haiti.
propositions.quote: She was asked whether someone could pick her up at the airport if she had to return to Haiti, and she answered yes, by making arrangements in advance.

propositions.text: Panel opines claimant has means to avoid arriving alone at Port-au-Prince airport.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant has the means to make sure that she is not alone when she arrives at the airport in Port-au-Prince.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant fears arriving alone but has arranged pickups and can avoid arriving alone at Port-au-Prince airport.

propositions.text: Claimant has family very involved in her life, including financial help from sisters and support after break and enter in 2017.
propositions.quote: The claimant also has family that appears to be very involved in her life. Her sisters provided her with financial help. She was able to move in with her family in XXXX in 1991, after her stepfather's disappearance, and was later taken care of after the break and enter at her home in 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant's family is very involved, providing financial help and support after break and enter.

propositions.text: Employer offered claimant an apartment in Port-au-Prince before she left for Canada.
propositions.quote: Her employer even offered her an apartment in Port-au-Prince for a period of time before she left for Canada.

propositions.text: Ms. XXXX cared for claimant's daughter during her US trips; daughter currently lives with Ms. XXXX.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX has looked after her daughter each time the claimant traveled to the United States. Her daughter is currently living with Ms. XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant's employer offered an apartment and Ms. XXXX cared for her daughter, who now lives with Ms. XXXX.

propositions.text: Despite living alone with daughter, claimant has strong family and social network supporting her.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that even though the claimant lives alone with her daughter, she has a strong family and social network looking out for her.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant has strong family and social support despite living alone with her daughter.

propositions.text: Claimant stated criminals who robbed her in 2015 were same as those demanding money at market but did not know them.
propositions.quote: The claimant also stated that she believed that the criminals who robbed her in 2015 were the same criminals who demanded money from her at the market. She did not know the criminals who robbed her.

propositions.text: Panel opines claimant is speculating about identity of criminals.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant is speculating.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant believes same criminals robbed and extorted her but is speculating about their identity.

propositions.text: Being victim of random crimes in 2015 and 2017 insufficient to prove personal risk of life or cruel treatment under IRPA if returned to Haiti.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that being the victim of a random crime in 2015 and in 2017 is not sufficient to establish, on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant would be personally subjected to a risk to her life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment under paragraph 97(1)(b) of the IRPA if she were to return to her country.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds random crimes in 2015 and 2017 do not establish personal risk under IRPA if claimant returns to Haiti.

propositions.text: Claimant's lawyer argues claimant would be perceived to have money after living in Canada, increasing risk if returned to Haiti.
propositions.quote: The claimant's lawyer argues that, if she were to return to Haiti, she would be perceived to have money after having lived in Canada.

propositions.text: Federal Court in Prophète ruled all Haitians face same risk regarding perception of money after living abroad.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court previously ruled on this type of argument in Prophète and concluded that all Haitians face the same risk.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's lawyer argues risk from perceived wealth; Federal Court in Prophète ruled all Haitians face same risk.

propositions.text: Panel determines claimant is not a Convention refugee under section 96 IRPA or person in need of protection under subsection 97(1) IRPA.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: Panel rejects refugee protection claim of claimant.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, the panel rejects the refugee protection claim of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim.
